title: Infinitesimal simplicity of restricted highest-weight modules
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] of characteristic $p>0$. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and such that every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Here solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial, and finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting with all elements after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ with unipotent radical $U$, character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, positive roots in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, coroots and pairing as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $V$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional rational $S$-module, meaning an $F$-vector space with a coassociative counital coaction $c_V:V\to V\otimes_F F[S]$. Assume it is simple: its only subspaces $N$ with $c_V(N)\subseteq N\otimes_F F[S]$ are $0$ and $V$. Suppose $V^U=\{v:c_V|_U(v)=v\otimes1\}$ is a one-dimensional line on which $T$ acts by a character $\lambda\in X$ after every commutative $F$-algebra extension, and that
$$0\leq\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle<p\qquad(\alpha\in\Delta).$$
Write $\epsilon:F[S]\to F$ for evaluation at the identity and define $\mathfrak s=\operatorname{Lie}(S)$ as the space of $F$-linear maps $x:F[S]\to F$ satisfying $x(ab)=\epsilon(a)x(b)+x(a)\epsilon(b)$. Its differential action on $V$ is $d\rho_V(x)=(1_V\otimes x)c_V$. Then every $F$-linear subspace $N\subseteq V$ satisfying $d\rho_V(x)N\subseteq N$ for all $x\in\mathfrak s$ is $0$ or $V$. The assertion includes $p=2$, the trivial group, zero highest weight and products of semisimple simply connected groups.

Corroboration read online: J. C. Jantzen, Moment graphs and representations, Sem. Congres 24 (2010), sections 5.1--5.2, printed pp.302--303, Curtis theorem, https://math.au.dk/~jantzen/grnbl.pdf. Full book reference WANTED: Jantzen (2003), Part II, sections 3.14--3.15.

proof.text: Choose $0\ne v\in V^U$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], $S$ is reductive and $B=U\rtimes T$, so $v$ is a $B$-eigenvector of weight $\lambda$. Its cyclic rational $S$-submodule is nonzero, hence is $V$ by simplicity. Apply [lem-sfb-primitive-cyclic-weight-bound] to obtain $V_\lambda=Fv$.

proof.text: Let $A$ be the unital $F$-subalgebra of $\operatorname{End}_F(V)$ generated by $d\rho_V(\mathfrak s)$, and put $D=Av$. The identity $\rho(g)\rho(1+\varepsilon x)\rho(g)^{-1}=\rho(1+\varepsilon\operatorname{Ad}_g x)$ over dual numbers gives $\rho(g)d\rho(x)\rho(g)^{-1}=d\rho(\operatorname{Ad}_g x)$. It holds after every scalar extension; tangent spaces base change since they are the duals of the finite-dimensional augmentation ideal modulo its square. Conjugation therefore normalizes the generated algebra $A_R$ for every $R$. By [lem-sfb-normalized-algebra-weight-line-simple], applied to the one-dimensional weight space in step 1, $D$ is a simple $A$-module.

source.place: Agent proof of 22.54, using the cited normalized-algebra and rank-one inputs; the restricted condition is on simple-coroot pairings.

proof.text: For each simple root $\alpha$, [lem-sfb-opposite-root-sl2-parametrizations] supplies a group-scheme map $v_\alpha:\operatorname{SL}_2\to S$ identifying its upper and lower unitriangular subgroups with $U_\alpha$ and $U_{-\alpha}$ and its diagonal with $\alpha^\vee$. By [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates], $U_\alpha\subseteq U$, so the upper subgroup fixes $v$. The pulled-back diagonal weight is the integer $m_\alpha=\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle$, with $0\le m_\alpha<p$. Apply [lem-sfb-sl2-highest-orbit-polynomial] to the pulled-back representation. If $f_\alpha$ is the lower differential, it belongs to $d\rho(\mathfrak s)\subseteq A$, and the formula $x_-(a)v=\sum_{j=0}^{m_\alpha}a^j(j!)^{-1}f_\alpha^jv$ shows $U_{-\alpha}(R)v\subseteq D_R$ for every $R$. Upper root elements fix $v$.

source.place: Agent proof of 22.54, using the cited normalized-algebra and rank-one inputs; the restricted condition is on simple-coroot pairings.

proof.text: For $t\in T(R)$, $tv=\lambda(t)v$. For each upper or lower simple root element $u$, step 3 gives $uv\in D_R$. Normalization from step 2 gives $g(Av)_R=(gA_Rg^{-1})(gv)\subseteq D_R$ for these $g$; apply this also to $g^{-1}$ to get equality. To pass to the whole group, choose a basis of $D$ and extend it to $V$. Inside $S$, impose that the lower-left matrix blocks of both $\rho(g)$ and $\rho(g^{-1})$ vanish. These are finitely many regular equations; their zero locus $K$ is a closed subgroup scheme, with $K(R)$ exactly the elements preserving $D_R$ in both directions. It contains $T$ and all $U_{\pm\alpha}$ for simple $\alpha$. By [lem-sfb-simple-root-generation-mixed-commutation], $K=S$. Evaluating this preservation at the universal element of $S(F[S])$ gives $c_V(D)\subseteq D\otimes_FF[S]$.

source.place: Agent proof of 22.54, using the cited normalized-algebra and rank-one inputs; the restricted condition is on simple-coroot pairings.

proof.text: The rational submodule $D$ contains $v\ne0$, so $D=V$. Step 2 says this is a simple $A$-module. If $N\subseteq V$ is stable under every $d\rho(x)$, it is stable under products, sums, scalar multiples and the identity, hence under the algebra $A$ they generate. Therefore $N=0$ or $N=V$. The argument divides only by $j!$ for $j<p$ and so includes $p=2$. Empty simple-root sets use the empty-root case $S=T$ of step 4; zero highest weight gives degree-zero polynomials; products require no additional argument.
